video_title: How the Democrats Did It | The Ezra Klein Show
gist: Ezra Klein and Michelle Goldberg analyze the 2026 Democratic midterm wave, including wins in Texas, Georgia, Kansas, Michigan, South Carolina and Mississippi. They argue the winners shared an anti-oligarchy, anti-corruption, affordability-focused populism, often aimed at tech billionaires and AI data centers, and that Trump's immigration crackdown reversed Hispanic gains and made the South unreliable for Republicans.

insights.claim: Rural Texans opposed AI data center buildout because of noise, eyesores, livestock harm and collapsing property values, and Democrats ran directly against data centers in the 2026 midterms.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Local opposition to data centers is now a proven winning political issue, raising siting, permitting and political risk for hyperscaler and data center capex.
insights.quote: They're loud. Like you talk to people who can no longer sleep at night who say that the noise is like killing their livestock

insights.claim: Some Texans living near data center construction say they cannot sell their homes because property values have fallen through the floor.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Data center externalities are being framed as property-value destruction, a potent grievance for local opposition and litigation.
insights.quote: they want to move but they can't sell their property cuz their property value has um fallen through the floor

insights.claim: Goldberg argues people tolerate sacrifices for an industry they expect to benefit from, but resent sacrifices for AI or crypto mining that tech leaders frame as 'get on board or be left behind' while warning it could destroy the world.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: The AI industry's messaging is a political liability; perceived lack of local benefit fuels backlash against AI infrastructure.
insights.quote: it's one thing to make sacrifices for an industry that you think you're going to benefit from. It's another to make sacrifices for like a crypto mine.

insights.claim: Gina Hinojosa's winning Texas governor campaign promised to cancel contracts that jeopardize the state's water supply, explicitly targeting data centers and billionaires.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: A Democratic Texas governor elected on anti-data-center water rhetoric could mean contract reviews and tougher water/permitting terms for Texas data center projects.
insights.quote: who will cancel contracts that jeopardize our water that we need to drink and live in our homes

insights.claim: Jon Ossoff attacked Mike Collins for voting to redirect health-care money to data center developers and demanded he commit to repealing what Ossoff called the 'data center tax scam.'
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Data center tax incentives are becoming a national campaign target; subsidies and tax breaks for data centers face repeal risk.
insights.quote: I want to know if you will commit to voting to repeal that data center tax scam that you voted for.

insights.claim: Sherrod Brown won the Ohio Senate seat running a very anti-data-center campaign, among other issues.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Anti-data-center politics worked in the Midwest as well as Texas, so the backlash is not regional.
insights.quote: Sher Brown won running uh again a very anti-data center campaign

insights.claim: Tech billionaires, especially Elon Musk after moving to Texas, became the face of the Republican party there, and Talarico seemed to run as much against Musk as against Ken Paxton.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Close identification of tech leaders with Trump-era Republicans makes Big Tech a bipartisan-populist political target.

insights.claim: Goldberg says upper-middle-class voters who once saw Silicon Valley as a Democratic stronghold now view Elon Musk and the tech bros as forces of inequality and 'incipient totalitarianism.'
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: The Democrats' former tech-friendly educated base has turned against the tech industry, so Democratic tech policy may get tougher.
insights.quote: They seem to be like the forces of not just inequality, but incipient totalitarianism.

insights.claim: Polls now show voters seeing the Republican party as the elitist party, which was not true a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Republicans losing the anti-elite mantle reshapes the coalition math in favor of Democratic populism.
insights.quote: People now in polls see the Republican party as the elitist party. That was not true a few years ago

insights.claim: In the 2026 Texas elections Democrats won the governorship, four of the five redistricted House seats, and made huge gains in the Texas House, beyond Talarico's Senate win.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: The Texas result was a broad wave, not a one-candidate fluke, signaling a durable shift in the largest red state.
insights.quote: Democrats won four of the five redistricted house seats. They won for governor. They had huge gains in the Texas House.

insights.claim: Texas border counties swung massively to Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential election: Cameron County +44, Hidalgo +49 and Webb +50.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Hispanic voters reversed their 2024 Trump shift, undoing the GOP's most important electoral gain.
insights.quote: Cameron County plus 44 swing to the Democrats. Hidalgo plus 49, Web plus 50.

insights.claim: Klein says Democrats look on track for 250 to 260 House seats after the 2026 midterms.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: A large Democratic House majority means aggressive oversight and investigations of the administration through 2028.
insights.quote: Democrats look to be on track for 250 to 260 House seats.

insights.claim: Jon Ossoff beat Mike Collins by 18 points in Georgia in a seat that was supposed to be endangered.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: A strong anti-corruption message produced a landslide in a swing state.
insights.quote: John Of crushed Mike Collins by 18 points.

insights.claim: Democrats look to have won Senate races in South Carolina and Mississippi, and Adam Hamilton won in Kansas, which had not had a Democratic senator since the 1930s.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: The Republican southern and plains base can no longer be taken for granted.
insights.quote: The last time Kansas had a Democrat in the Senate was the 1930s.

insights.claim: Klein frames the result as a 'dealignment' rather than a realignment: the South is now unreliable for Republicans, who will have to spend to defend it, turning the 2028 map back into an open map of states.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: A wider battlefield spreads GOP resources thin and shapes 2028 presidential strategy and campaign spending.
insights.quote: I think of this more as a deignment. >> What has happened is the South has become unreliable now for the Republican party. They have to defend it.

insights.claim: Gina Hinojosa argued Texas was winnable this time because Democrats fielded serious candidates up and down the ballot, which compounds turnout, unlike Beto O'Rourke's lone 2018 run.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Contesting every race, not relying on one marquee candidate, multiplies a wave.
insights.quote: because this time we have a ticket like because this time we have a team.

insights.claim: Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Senate race by about seven points, roughly the margin he predicted, though that may slightly underperform the rest of the Democratic field.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: A hard-left populist can win a Rust Belt Senate race, though how much it cost at the margin is unclear.

insights.claim: Goldberg says Trump won new Mexican-American voters in Texas and then 'terrorized them' by handing immigration policy to Stephen Miller, Greg Bovino and Kristi Noem, which drove the Hispanic swing back to Democrats.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Aggressive deportation enforcement destroyed the GOP's Hispanic gains, a lasting electoral cost of the policy.
insights.quote: Donald Trump got a bunch of new voters among um mostly [clears throat] Mexican-American people in Texas and then he absolutely terrorized them.

insights.claim: Goldberg argues the assumption that diversity automatically benefits Democrats was wrong, but that ICE raids on relatives at job sites created a backlash that rhetoric alone never did.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Demographics are not destiny; direct policy harm, not identity appeals, moves these voters.
insights.quote: it's another thing to have masked men grabbing your relatives off their job sites

insights.claim: School vouchers are a sleeper issue: rural Texas parents and even MAGA voters, including a former school superintendent, turned on Greg Abbott because vouchers were defunding public schools and cutting services like after-school busing.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Voucher programs carry political risk in rural areas without private-school options.
insights.quote: this is maybe a kind of a sleeper issue in a lot of places

insights.claim: Ossoff turned Trump's corruption into a winning message by tying it to voters' costs; for example, he said that after Eric Trump and Don Jr. took a stake in a company pursuing a Kazakh tungsten mining deal, the US government set aside $1.6 billion to finance the project.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Government-financed critical-minerals deals tied to the Trump family are now oversight targets for a Democratic Congress.
insights.quote: Kazakhstan announces this company will get quote, "the largest known undeveloped tungsten resource in the world."

insights.claim: Klein says Ossoff showed that Trump's corruption, long assumed to be a vulnerability that never landed, can be turned into viral, almost unanswerable clips.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Expect Democrats nationally to center the 'Mar-a-Lago mafia' corruption message and investigations through 2028.
insights.quote: Oaf was the one who was able to weaponize the insight

insights.claim: Goldberg compares Ossoff to Hungary's Péter Magyar, who combined reclaimed national identity with a relentless focus on Orbán's corruption and tied elite self-enrichment to voters' own suffering.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: An anti-corruption-plus-patriotism playbook is beating entrenched populist-right governments across countries.
insights.quote: It's not just that they're enriching themselves, but they're doing it at your expense.

insights.claim: Goldberg predicts the new Congress will be divided between holding Trump accountable and moving forward, with corruption investigations as the overlap, and she would be very surprised if Democrats could raise taxes or pass a wealth tax soon.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Expect investigations, not major tax legislation; near-term risk of a wealth tax is low.
insights.quote: I would be very surprised if they're able to say raise taxes or institute a wealth tax anytime soon.

themes.theme: Healthcare as the next Democratic agenda

insights.claim: Abdul El-Sayed ran on Medicare for All, and it barely registered as a line of attack; Klein says Medicare for All has never polled as well as it does this year.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Single-payer is no longer an electoral liability, raising long-run policy risk for insurers.
insights.quote: It is a reflection of where the healthare system right now is that Medicare for all has never pulled as well as it has this year.

insights.claim: Goldberg expects El-Sayed to focus most on expanding Medicare, which she calls very popular, and Klein expects healthcare reform to be revisited before 2028 as doctors like El-Sayed and Annie Andrews join the Senate.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Healthcare reform and Medicare expansion are likely central 2028 issues, a policy overhang for managed care.
insights.quote: the thing we're going to hear Abdul say talk about the most, my guess, is expanding Medicare.

insights.claim: Goldberg says Democrats might be able to restore the ACA subsidies even with Trump in office.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: ACA subsidy restoration is a possible near-term bipartisan deal that would matter for exchange-focused insurers.
insights.quote: They might be able to restore the ACA subsidies

insights.claim: James Talarico won Texas by combining a faith-based 'love your neighbor' politics with an everyone-against-the-billionaires populism, and moderated on oil and gas, some trans issues and border enforcement.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: The winning template is cultural warmth plus economic populism, with moderation on energy and the border, which lowers anti-oil-and-gas risk from Texas Democrats.
insights.quote: So it's this kind of like everyone against the billionaires kind of politics which just is numerically um much better than a sort of like red blue divide.

insights.claim: Klein credits Joe Rogan's interview and praise of Talarico with convincing Democrats that his approach could reach persuadable voters.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Appearing in non-partisan or right-leaning media is now seen as a validated Democratic strategy.
insights.quote: You got to give Joe Rogan some credit here.

insights.claim: Hinojosa said the voters Democrats would win were not country-club Republicans but MAGA voters, a break from the 2018-2024 theory of targeting educated suburbanites.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: The Democratic coalition strategy is pivoting toward working-class Trump voters and economic grievances.
insights.quote: the people that we're going to win are not the country club Republicans, it's MAGA.

insights.claim: Goldberg theorizes that voters reward the side that seems to care less about a culture-war issue; Kamala Harris was hurt by trans issues in 2024 because of what they signaled about her priorities.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Culture-war issues are losing their pull compared with cost-of-living and corruption messaging.
insights.quote: I also have a theory that voters reward the side that seems to care about that issue less.

insights.claim: Goldberg says abortion-rights referendums drive turnout but do not necessarily get people to vote for Democrats, and may have given voters permission to vote Republican once their rights were protected.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: Abortion is a weaker partisan lever than assumed, so Democrats are leaning more on economic issues.
insights.quote: some of these referendums kind of gave people um permission to vote for Republicans because they had protected their abortion rights.

insights.claim: Klein argues the Democratic establishment's sense of electability needs updating because it does not select for star power, charisma or authentic movements, as shown by the Schumer-backed Haley Stevens, who later endorsed the Republican.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Insurgent, high-energy candidates are outperforming establishment picks, shifting power within the party.
insights.quote: is it does not care about and does not select for star power.

insights.claim: Winning campaigns kept bringing every attack back to affordability: gas, groceries and healthcare costs.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living pressure is the dominant voter concern and will drive policy priorities.
insights.quote: we all know that my name and my faith aren't the reason you can't afford your gas.

insights.claim: Goldberg says the core difference between the 2026 and 2018 Democratic classes is a focus on oligarchy and corruption, positioning Democrats as the anti-elite, anti-corporate, anti-billionaire party.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: A Democratic Party branded as anti-corporate means more regulatory and oversight risk for large companies and billionaire-linked firms.
insights.quote: it has created the conditions for Democrats to be the anti- elite kind of anti-corporate, anti-billionaire class.

insights.claim: Klein says that unlike 2018, Democrats no longer see Trumpism as an aberration; after 2024 they are wary of using power in ways that push voters back to the other side.
insights.speaker: Ezra Klein
insights.so_what: Expect more cautious, popularity-focused governing by Democrats, not maximalist policy.

insights.claim: Goldberg says the Republican coalition 'has evaporated overnight' and the party must rethink how to be a conservative party in a multiracial democracy as Trump exits, questioning whether JD Vance could win a no-longer-safe state like Mississippi.
insights.speaker: Michelle Goldberg
insights.so_what: The GOP's 2028 succession and strategy are newly uncertain.
